content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to programming and working on a small hotel project with 20 rooms. I need to receive the status of an input from each room and display this status on a webserver. The main area device will act as the webserver. I've structured the network as shown in the attached images: each room device sends its input status via the network to an area controller, and each area controller sends to the main area controller. Is this setup possible? All controllers will be configured as masters. Are there any limitations when it comes to communication?
This can be done. However, what is the purpose of the flags you're using?
Thank you for your answer. I assumed the flags were necessary for visualization. Is there another way to achieve this?
Instead of showing the state of the flags, you could display the states of the network inputs.
I will try to adjust my setup. Previously, I used flags, since within the block type in the editor, only certain options are available.
Let me create an example for you.
On all controllers with version [version_no], you need to enable S7 access.
Alright, you should configure the network inputs and outputs for remote settings, not for local memory purposes. That means you can use the memory flags only.
Thanks for your assistance. Your advice was beneficial and I’ll run some tests in the coming days.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is setting up a distributed network of [company_name] controllers for hotel room status visualization with a webserver. The discussion covers uncertainty regarding memory flags, network inputs/outputs, and options in the web editor. The primary concern is achieving reliable, real-time remote visualization from several controller modules and understanding any potential communication limits or recommended practices.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a simple method for remotely visualizing multiple distributed inputs with a clear network setup and no unexpected communication restrictions.
